artworks.title: Teiresias Foretells the Future to Odysseus
artworks.description: Fuseli's Nekyia: the blind Theban seer rises among the shades to speak to Odysseus — the underworld oracle of the Odyssey rendered in Romantic storm-light.

artworks.title: Tiresias Transformed into a Woman
artworks.description: A Venetian Baroque reading of the metamorphosis: Tiresias, having struck the coupling snakes, stands changed — the prophet who would know both sexes before Hera struck him blind.

artworks.title: Odysseus Takes Counsel with Teiresias
artworks.description: Abildgaard's Copenhagen canvas from Homer's Nekyia: Odysseus leans toward the blind prophet among the dead — the road home spoken in the dark of Hades.

artworks.title: Odysseus and Teiresias
artworks.description: A Dutch Mannerist sheet now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington: Odysseus consults the shade of Tiresias — the Homeric interview distilled to two figures and a prophetic staff.

artworks.title: Manto and Tiresias
artworks.description: Singleton's National Gallery canvas: the blind seer guided by his daughter Manto — prophecy as a family craft, sightless father and seeing child on the road from Thebes.

films.title: Oedipus the King
films.description: Orson Welles' Tiresias is the blind seer who will not speak until forced — the prophet who already knows the king's crime.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky keeps Tiresias in the underworld Nekyia — the Theban seer who tells Odysseus how to get home, still blind, still certain.

music.title: Oedipus Rex
music.description: Stravinsky's Tiresias delivers the oracle in Latin granite — the blind voice that turns the opera-oratorio toward recognition.
